name: מְרָרִי
summary: The third son of Levi (with Gershon and Kohath), who went down to Egypt with Jacob; his sons Mahli and Mushi were the Merarite clans. They camped north of the Dwelling and carried its boards, bars, pillars and sockets, with four wagons for them, and with the sons of Gershon set out carrying the Dwelling (Num 10:17); they received twelve cities from Reuben, Gad and Zebulun. The name is the letters of מָרַר “be bitter” with the ending ‑ִי, as in the adjective מְרִירִי “bitter” (Deu 32:24), so “bitter” or “my bitterness”; scripture gives no reason for it.

evidence.note: “The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath וּמְרָרִי.”
The sons of Levi by their generations.
“The sons of מְרָרִי: Mahli and Mushi.”
The Merarite clans camp on the north side of the Dwelling and keep its boards, bars, pillars and sockets, and the pillars of the court.
The service of carrying the sons of Merari, under Ithamar.
Four wagons and eight oxen, “according to their service”.
“The Dwelling was taken down, and the sons of Gershon וּבְנֵי מְרָרִי set out, carrying the Dwelling.”
לִמְרָרִי מִשְׁפַּחַת הַמְּרָרִי, of Merari the clan of the Merarite.
Twelve cities from Reuben, Gad and Zebulun.
The root’s adjective with the same ending: קֶטֶב מְרִירִי, bitter destruction.
The root’s verb: כִּי־מַר־לִי מְאֹד, “it is very bitter to me”.

note: bdb includes the gentilic הַמְּרָרִי (m.dq.aq, Num 26:57), which TIPNR files as a form of Merari@Gen.46.11, following names/gershon.json; drop it if gentilics should not be claimed by name entries. No verse explains the name. Merari was born before Israel went down to Egypt (Gen 46:11), so the name cannot look back to the bondage of Exo 1:14.
